note: ST I q.2 a.3 co., prima via, 'et hoc omnes intelligunt Deum', says that the first mover moved by none is what everyone understands as God. That is a report of how the name is used. The premise needs more: that a first mover which is pure act and the only first unmoved mover is God in the sense of the God of classical theism (DEF-GOD-OF-CLASSICAL-THEISM), which the sentence does not state (DISAMB-GOD). The sentence also does not use the pure-act and uniqueness antecedents. Aquinas argues the attributes later (ST I qq.3-26, candidate AQUINAS-ST-I-Q3-Q26-IDENTIFICATION), so the premise is to be derived from them, not read off a single sentence.
